valuation_philosophy.model_type: REIT sum-of-parts blended with group AFFO capitalisation at the cost of equity -- NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.routing: dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'REIT / property trust (IAS 40 fair-value, external manager)' -> AFFO / distributable-profit capitalisation at cost of equity; plus the 'straddles two rows' rule (a REIT with an operating funds-management business) -> value the parts and sum. Fresh build; no prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_owner_fcf: Stride is a stapled security: SPL (property owner, ~$900m direct office/town-centre book plus $356m of equity-accounted stakes in Investore 18.8%, Industre 49.0%, Diversified 2.2%) stapled to SIML (external funds manager, $22.9m external fees on ~$2.4bn external AUM). Reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised IAS 40 revaluations (+$112.3m FY2022, -$116.7m FY2023, -$56.1m FY2024); statutory EPS and P/E are meaningless. Reported FCF (OCF less capex) treats discretionary development spend as a running cost and ignores the $114m Silverdale recycling. EBITDA is undefined. The company's own distributable profit / AFFO -- profit before tax stripped of fair-value moves and equity-accounted profit, plus cash dividends from the associates, less current tax, less maintenance capex and incentives -- is the owner-earnings series, and it is measured AFTER interest, so it is capitalised at the COST OF EQUITY and net debt is never deducted again.
valuation_philosophy.sum_of_parts_vs_blended: CHOICE: a 50/50 blend of (1) group AFFO capitalisation and (2) a sum-of-parts asset leg (property NTA x exit P/NTA + SIML at a fund-manager multiple + PV of dividends). Reasons for including the sum-of-parts rather than a plain AFFO+NTA blend: NTA ($1.69) is essentially SPL's property equity -- SIML contributes 4c of net assets against ~$9.6m of after-tax earnings -- so a P/NTA anchor alone prices the manager at 2.5x earnings, which is why Stride traded at ~1.0x NTA in FY2017-21 (the market capitalised the platform) while peers sat at 0.85x. Reasons for NOT relying on sum-of-parts alone: the segment distributable-profit split is not disclosed; ~40% of SIML's stand-alone profit is fees charged to SPL; the fee leg faces a dated mandate review and internalisation risk that a static earnings multiple understates; and summing parts is the classic way a REIT ends up valued above what its cash earnings support. Leg 1 (one flow, one rate) is the discipline on leg 2. Both legs are computed per scenario and the blend is 50/50.
valuation_philosophy.diversified_review_treatment: The 2026 Diversified 10-year review is treated as a base-case EVENT, not a risk premium: the base AFFO and SIML paths assume the fund is wound up (management's 5-6% DPPS estimate, phased FY2028-29 with project/termination fees offsetting in FY2027-28). A 0.40% mandate/internalisation premium in the cost of equity covers the broader, undated risk that Investore or Industre re-tender -- that premium is charged once, in the rate, and the Diversified loss once, in the flows.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Base blended value NZ$0.98 (AFFO leg 0.85, sum-of-parts leg 1.10) against a NZ$1.09 price; probability-weighted NZ$0.99. The AFFO leg says the stock is fully priced for its cash earnings at an 11% cost of equity; the asset leg says the parts are worth more than the group trades for even after a Diversified wind-up. The blend lands close to the price -- a mature income vehicle at the bottom of its 10-year range, roughly fairly valued for yield, with the Diversified vote and the H2-2027 office recovery as the two dated swing factors.

warnings: This is a REIT sum-of-parts / AFFO-capitalisation model at the cost of equity, NOT an owner-FCF DCF. Reported NetIncome (FY2023 -$116.7m, FY2024 -$56.1m, FY2022 +$112.3m) is IAS 40 revaluation noise; reported FreeCashFlow nets discretionary development/acquisition capex; EBITDA is undefined under fair-value accounting. None of them drives the valuation.

AFFO, distributable profit and NTA are all post-debt. Net debt ($278.6m at 31-Mar-2026) is recorded for audit only and is NEVER subtracted from any leg -- doing so would double-count leverage already inside the flows and the book value.

DATED EVENT: the Diversified NZ Property Fund reaches its 10-year review in calendar 2026. Management discloses that a wind-up would cut normalised distributable profit ~5-6%. The BASE case assumes the wind-up happens (fee loss phased FY2028-29, ~$2.7m after tax); only the bull case retains the mandate. The outcome should be known by the FY2027 interim (Nov-2026) -- refresh this DCF against it.

The 8.0c dividend is 105% of FY2026 AFFO (7.60c) and 91% of distributable profit (8.78c); the ~$6.6m/yr of maintenance capex and incentives sits between the two. Base holds 8.0c flat for five years (FY2027 guidance); bear cuts to 7.0c. There is no per-share growth in the dividend until AFFO coverage is restored.

Investore stake: carried at $87.1m under equity accounting against a $74.3m market value at 31-Mar-2026 (SPL relies on a 17.5% 'strategic premium' to avoid a further impairment beyond the $2.1m taken). A mark-to-market is -2.3c of NTA; charged in the bear NTA path only.

SIML's stand-alone profit ($13.4m PBT) includes ~$10.2m of fees charged to SPL. That is a genuine management cost SPL's AFFO already bears, so valuing SIML on its stand-alone NPAT alongside SPL's AFFO does not double count -- but it does mean roughly 40% of the manager's economics are captive to the group's own balance sheet.

Share count held FLAT at 559.462m: SBC ($1.6m net) is expensed inside distributable profit and the DRP has not been material (559.0m -> 559.5m FY2025-26). Diluted weighted count is 563.747m (+0.8%) -- immaterial, stated rather than modelled.

The dashboard slider engine cannot rebuild a two-leg REIT model from owner-FCF component fields; expect the generic scaler (FALLBACK) as on ARG.NZ / IPL.NZ / PCT.NZ. The recorded assumptions are complete enough to recompute every number in this file by hand.

Price NZ$1.09 is the 2-Sep-2026 NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime 05:00:13Z), a fresh print, at the bottom of the 52-week range (1.055-1.53). Balance-sheet anchors (NTA, debt, shares) are 31-Mar-2026; post-balance-date sales (Woolworths Greenlane $35.9m) are in the FY2027 driver judgments, not the anchors.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case forward AFFO/share CAGR FY2026-FY2031 (7.60c -> 7.94c). No historical CAGR is a usable forward proxy: AFFO/share fell 6.8%/yr over FY2021-26 on the rate cycle, the FY2021-22 equity raises and the Silverdale/Industre restructure, and the forward path is dominated by a dated event (the 2026 Diversified review) rather than a trend. Stored as a percent for the screener.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-4.2%/yr FY2023-26) and revenue CAGR (-1.9%/yr) both describe a shrinking balance sheet as SPL recycled assets (Silverdale $114m to Investore, Woolworths sites) and wrote property values down (FY2023 -$116.7m, FY2024 -$56.1m NPAT). EPS and reported-FCF CAGRs are not computed: statutory EPS is IAS 40 revaluation noise (-21.6c FY2023 to +22.7c FY2022) and reported FCF is net of discretionary development/acquisition capex. Per-share AFFO and NTA are the honest series.
historical_growth.notes: Per-share AFFO peaked at 10.83c in FY2021 and is 30% lower today; roughly half of that decline is share issuance (365m -> 559m shares FY2020-FY2024, the FY2021-22 raises funding Industre/Investore stakes) and half is higher funding costs (weighted cost of debt 3.6% -> 5.0%) and the office cycle. External management fee income, the SIML leg, is the one growing series: 8.5m -> 22.9m over nine years (11.6%/yr) though flat since FY2021 (25.1m -> 22.9m) as Diversified's development activity faded.

cost_of_equity_build.risk_free_rate_note: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5-4.7% (Aug/Sep-2026); RBNZ raised the OCR to 2.50% in July 2026 with further hikes flagged, so the long end is biased up. Same basis as PCT.NZ (Aug-2026) for comparability.
cost_of_equity_build.beta_note: NZ listed-property beta below 1.0 (contracted rent, 95% group occupancy, 6.6yr WALT) but above PCT's 0.80: 34% bank LVR / 35% look-through, an office-heavy direct book at 85.7% occupancy, and ~NZ$610m market cap.
cost_of_equity_build.office_structural_premium_note: ~78% of SPL's directly held book ($706m of ~$900m) is Auckland/Wellington office at 85.7% occupancy with cap rates that softened 5.9% -> 6.2% in FY2026 and no recovery guided before H2 CY2027.
cost_of_equity_build.mandate_internalisation_premium_note: SIML's fee leg (~21% of look-through revenue, ~25% of group DP) depends on capital partners continuing to appoint it: the Diversified 10-year review is a dated 2026 event (5-6% of DPPS), and Investore (NZX-listed, 18.8% SPL-owned) and Industre (JPMAM JV) can internalise or re-tender. Charged once here, in the discount rate; the Diversified loss itself is charged in the base AFFO/SIML paths, not again in the rate.
cost_of_equity_build.illiquidity_ns_premium_note: NZX small cap outside the NZX 50 core, thin turnover, and the Non-Standard (NS) listing designation on the stapled security that some index/institutional mandates exclude. IPL.NZ carries the same class of premium.
cost_of_equity_build.governance_related_party_premium_note: SPL sells assets to (Silverdale, $114m) and co-invests in the vehicles SIML manages; cross-holdings and a Chair transition at the 2026 AGM. Small, explicit, so it is not smuggled into beta.
cost_of_equity_build.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY, not WACC -- AFFO, distributable profit and NTA are all post-debt, so the debt cost is already inside the flow and the book value. Built in NZD off the NZ risk-free rate, matching NZD flows and the NZD quote. Base 11.0% = CAPM 9.7% (4.6% + 0.85 x 6.0%) + 0.35% office + 0.40% mandate/internalisation + 0.40% illiquidity/NS + 0.15% governance. Above ARG (9.5%), PCT (10.25%) and IPL (10.5%) because Stride layers a fee business with a dated mandate risk on top of an office-heavy book at a smaller scale; a levered NZ property vehicle must clear well more than its 7.3% dividend yield.

base.wacc_note: This is the COST OF EQUITY, stored under `wacc` only so the screener and dashboard find the discount rate. AFFO is post-interest; no blended WACC is used anywhere in the model.
base.terminal_value_rule: TV = min( AFFO_5 x (1+g) / (CoE - g) , AFFO_5 / exit_affo_yield ). The exit-yield multiple is a CAP on the Gordon value, exactly as terminal_cap_multiple works in the owner-FCF engine; it binds only when the discount rate falls below roughly CoE-1pp. Entry price and required-return rows rebuild the Gordon value at their own rate.
base.rationale: AFFO/share FY2027 +1.5%: full-year interest saving on the $114m Silverdale proceeds and $35.9m Woolworths Greenlane sale (debt 5.0% vs the ~6.5-6.8% yields sold, roughly neutral on AFFO), Industre's Favona Road and Wickham Street developments now income-producing and adding recurring fees, activity fees from the ~$70m Patiki Road build, and Diversified project/termination fees in the near term. FY2028 -2.0% and FY2029 -1.0%: the base case ASSUMES the Diversified NZ Property Fund IS wound up at its 2026 10-year review (management's own dated disclosure: 'unitholders may seek liquidity', impact 'around 5-6% of DPPS on a normalised basis'); the recurring fee (~$5.9m of closed-ended fee income) falls away as the assets sell through FY2028, the offsetting project fees roll off, and the full ~5.5% hit lands by FY2029 net of underlying growth. FY2030-31 +3.0%: office recovery from H2 CY2027 (management guides no material change before then) lifts 85.7% office occupancy toward 90%, rent reviews on 6.6yr WALT, and Investore/Industre fee growth. Terminal 2.5% (below NZ rent-escalator inflation, reflecting maintenance-capex leakage and the uncovered dividend). Exit AFFO yield 7.5% (13.3x) is a cap; at 11% CoE the Gordon value (12.1x) binds -- deliberately below the 13.6-14.6x the stock has traded at since FY2023 and far below the 21-25x of FY2021-22. NTA (property leg): -1.5%/-0.5% in FY2027-28 as office cap rates drift from 6.2% toward 6.4%, the Investore stake carries a further impairment ($87.1m book vs $74.3m market), and the 8.0c dividend exceeds 7.6c AFFO; +1.0/1.5/2.0% thereafter. Exit P/NTA 0.72x on the property leg -- above the ~0.57x the market implies for it today once SIML is stripped out, in line with the IPL.NZ base (0.75x), and BELOW the 0.66x group-average P/NTA of FY2023-26 once SIML's separate value is added back. SIML: FY2026 stand-alone NPAT $9.6m -> $9.9m FY2027 (growth + Diversified termination fees) -> $8.0m FY2029 (net Diversified loss ~$2.7m after tax, matching management's 5-6% of group DP) -> $8.8m FY2031 at 4-5% AUM-driven growth; exit 9x after-tax earnings, a discount to listed fund-manager multiples for a captive-mandate manager with internalisation risk. Dividend HELD at 8.0c (FY2027 guidance; DP payout 91%, AFFO payout 105%).

bull.rationale: Diversified unitholders resolve to continue (or the fund is rolled into a successor Stride-managed vehicle), so no fee loss; RBNZ resumes easing after the July-2026 hike, cap rates stabilise then compress; Auckland office flight-to-quality lifts SPL's refurbished 34 Shortland Street / 215 Lambton Quay occupancy to 92%+; North Wharf consent lands 2027 and the Patiki Road / Investore convenience-retail pipeline grows external AUM toward $3bn, compounding recurring fees at ~7%/yr (SIML NPAT $13.4m by FY2031, 11x exit). AFFO/share +3.0-4.0%/yr, dividend resumes growth to 8.75c by FY2031, NTA +2.0-2.5%/yr, exit P/NTA 0.88x (below the ~1.0x of FY2017-21 when the market paid up for the SIML platform), exit AFFO yield 6.5% (15.4x cap; Gordon at 10%/3% = 14.7x binds). bear.wacc_note: This is the COST OF EQUITY, stored under `wacc` only so the screener and dashboard find the discount rate. AFFO is post-interest; no blended WACC is used anywhere in the model.

bear.rationale: Diversified is wound up AND the mandate-loss precedent spreads: Investore's independent directors re-base the SIML fee on internalisation grounds (the Silverdale related-party sale gives them the pretext), so SIML NPAT falls to $6.0m and is valued at 6x. Office does not recover before FY2029: occupancy slips below 85%, cap rates move to 6.6-6.8%, another year of negative revaluations (NTA -4%/-3%/-1.5%) and the Investore stake is marked to market (-2.3c). The 8.0c dividend is cut to 7.0c from FY2028 once the DP payout would exceed 100%. RBNZ keeps hiking (95% hedged today, but the hedge book rolls into FY2030 refinancing). AFFO/share -2/-5/-3/0/+1%, exit AFFO yield 8.5% (11.8x cap; Gordon at 12.5%/1.5% = 9.2x binds), exit P/NTA 0.55x -- the group has already traded at 0.64x, and stripping SIML's value out implies the market prices the property leg near 0.57x today. CoE 12.5%.

assumptions.blend_rationale: 50/50 between (1) the group AFFO-capitalisation leg -- the REIT convention (ARG/IPL/PCT precedent) applied to the ONE flow that already contains both SPL's rent and SIML's fees, so no segment split is needed -- and (2) the sum-of-parts asset leg: SPL's property NTA at a justified exit P/NTA plus SIML's fee business at a fund-manager earnings multiple plus PV of interim dividends. Leg 2 exists because NTA carries SIML at ~$24m of net assets (4c/share) while it earns ~$9.6m after tax; a P/NTA-only view would price the manager at 2.5x earnings. Leg 1 is the check on leg 2: if the parts sum to more than the group's cash earnings can support at the cost of equity, the blend pulls the answer back.

cross_checks.floor_basis: FY2026 AFFO 7.60c capitalised in perpetuity at 11.0% cost of equity, zero growth ever
cross_checks.dividend_policy: 80-100% of SPL distributable profit + 25-75% of SIML distributable profit; FY2026 combined payout 91.1% of group DP; FY2027 guidance 8.0cps
cross_checks.current_price_implied_cap_rate_note: Market P/NTA 0.645x prices group equity ~NZ$336m below book; loaded onto the ~$1.4bn look-through portfolio that is ~24% of asset value, i.e. the market prices roughly 6.2% -> ~7.5% cap rates OR a zero value for SIML plus ~100bp -- either way well beyond the FY2026 revaluation.

entry_price.basis: AFFO-capitalisation leg only, all three scenarios, probability-weighted (ARG/IPL/PCT precedent). Interim AFFO/share and the year-5 terminal value discounted at the 15% hurdle, with the terminal value REBUILT at the hurdle: TV = min( AFFO_5 x (1+g) / (0.15 - g) , AFFO_5 / exit_affo_yield ) -- the Gordon value at 15% binds in every scenario (7.9x base), the exit-yield cap never does. This is the post-2026-09-01 house rule (terminal value at the rate you discount at), not the pre-fix 'keep the CoE-built TV' variant. No net-debt adjustment: AFFO is post-interest.
entry_price.self_consistency_check: Recomputing the IRR of (pay entry_price, receive base AFFO/share FY2027-31, exit at a TV built at that same IRR) returns 15.0% by construction; the 15% row of required_return_table equals the base entry price and the 11% row equals valuation.affo_capitalization_leg.base.intrinsic_value.

required_return_table.basis: AFFO-capitalisation leg only; every row rebuilds its terminal value at that row's rate (min Gordon@r, 13.33x cap). The 11% row equals valuation.affo_capitalization_leg.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Blended IV is not rate-reproducible this way because the SOTP leg uses explicit exit multiples.

sensitivity.matrix_note: AFFO-capitalisation leg only, base AFFO path held constant, exit-yield cap fixed at 7.5% (13.33x). Rows = cost of equity 9-13%, columns = terminal growth 1.5-3.5%. NZ$ per security.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25. Base at 50%: the FY2027 dividend is guided, the debt book is termed out to FY2030 and 95% hedged, and the Diversified wind-up is already INSIDE the base case so the base is not a hope case. Bear held at a full 25% (not the house-default 15%): the mandate-loss precedent could spread to Investore, office occupancy is 85.7% with no recovery guided before H2 CY2027, the RBNZ has resumed hiking, and the dividend is uncovered against AFFO. Bull 25%: retaining Diversified plus an office recovery plus North Wharf is a real path, but two of those three are outside management's control.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapsed: SBC ($1.6m) is immaterial and already expensed inside AFFO, so house and street values coincide. band_position is null by design, not zero.

sanity_check.note: REIT model: multiples use company-disclosed AFFO/share and NTA/share, never GAAP EPS or EBITDA. P/E is skipped (statutory EPS swings -21.6c FY2023 to +22.7c FY2022 on IAS 40 revaluations) and EV/EBITDA is skipped (no clean D&A/EBIT split under fair-value accounting; EBITDA NULL in the Metrics CSV by design). P/B == P/NTA here because Stride carries no intangibles (equity 945.7m / 559.462m = $1.69 = NTA). The meaningful anchor is P/NTA against Stride's own 10-year history of 31-March closes (Yahoo 10y monthly) vs FY NTA.

price_range_10yr.current_position: at the bottom of the range (NZ$1.09 vs 10yr low 1.08; 52w 1.055-1.53)

implied_multiples_at_current_price.p_nta_property_leg_note: Market price less SIML at 9x FY2026 NPAT (15.4c), over property-leg NTA $1.647 -- what the market implies for the property leg if the manager is worth a fund-manager multiple.
implied_multiples_at_current_price.p_e_note: Skipped: statutory EPS is fair-value-revaluation noise

historical_averages_10yr.p_nta_note: Two regimes: FY2017-FY2021 the stapled security traded at 0.95-1.08x NTA (the market capitalised SIML's growing fee platform and the low-rate era; FY2020's 0.79x is the COVID March-2020 print), then FY2022 0.87x and a PERSISTENT 0.64-0.70x discount FY2023-FY2026 through the rate cycle, office downturn and NTA erosion ($2.28 -> $1.69). The current 0.645x is the cheapest FY-end reading in the history.
historical_averages_10yr.p_affo_note: P/AFFO 13.5-14.6x since FY2023 versus 19-23x at the FY2019-22 rate trough; the model's base exit multiple (12.1x Gordon, 13.3x cap) sits at or below the entire post-2022 range.

trip_thresholds.p_nta_premium_trip: any scenario IV implying > 1.0x group NTA, given the FY2023-26 persistent discount -- REIT-specific trip requested for this ticker
trip_thresholds.upside_trip: >100% upside while the price sits in the upper half of the 10yr range -- N/A: price is at the BOTTOM of the range and base upside is small

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base blended IV NZ$0.98 implies 0.58x group NTA -- a DISCOUNT, BELOW the FY2023-26 band (0.64-0.70x), below the current 0.645x and the 10yr average (0.84x); the bull case (0.77x) stays below the 0.95-1.08x of FY2017-21 and far below the 1.62x trip line. Implied P/AFFO at base IV (12.8x FY2026) is below the 13.5-14.6x post-2022 traded range and below the 35.2x trip. The model is conservative by construction: the AFFO leg's Gordon terminal (12.1x) is below anything the stock has traded at since FY2023, the base case assumes the Diversified mandate is LOST, the dividend is held flat, and SIML is capitalised at 9x -- below listed fund-manager multiples.
